messages:
sami: quick heads-up — after the kernel-affinity tweak on the non-chat embeddings/reranker endpoint we saw a subtle perf shift in continuous batching. low-level numbers first, then a proposed tweak.

jia: saw the alert, thanks. which tweak specifically? kernel selection pinned to ampere-optimized GEMM?

sami: yes — runtime now prefers kernel v2 for sparse attention patterns; we thought it would help long sequences but it seems to change batch formation slightly -> fewer early-fills for small token reqs.

mike: few clarifying points: is this about the token wallet / per-request token budget target math or queue shaping? can you paste the short profile?

sami: short dump from staging perf-run (10m window, heavy rerank non-chat workload):
```
requests: 12.3k
avg lat (p95): 84ms -> baseline 72ms
tokens/sec per GPU: 45k -> baseline 52k
batch sizes (median): 6 -> baseline 8
early-fill rate: 28% -> baseline 46%
kv-hit ratio: 0.73 -> baseline 0.74
kernel mix: v2 62% / v1 38% (baseline v1 88% / v2 12%)
```

ops-jen: interesting that kv-hit ratio didn't move much but tokens/sec dropped. sounds like batch formation skewed towards many small batches.

jia: kernel v2 has slightly higher per-token compute at short seqs (better throughput amortized at 128+ seqs). if runtime picks it for majority, small-batch penalty shows.

mike: that explains it. So continuous batcher heuristics (slot-sculptor) are sensitive to kernel selection because their target token-wallet drains slower/faster depending on kernel latency curve.

sami: exactly. current token-wallet target is fixed per-model: "wallet_target_tokens = 25600". when kernel latency profile shifts, effective slot fill rate changes -> early-fill fallback triggers less often.

perf-bot: regression detected: rts/emb-rerank nonchat: +16% p95 latency vs baseline (last 24h), flagged at 1799989000

ops-jen: proposal: 2-step mitigation
1) make wallet target adaptive: multiply by observed median per-token-latency factor for chosen kernel
2) add a small windowed early-fill override: if median batch size < 4 and p95 > threshold, force aggressive early-fill for next N slots

jia: sounds reasonable. any risk of overfilling GPU memory with step 2? we need a soft cap check against model kv cache size.

mike: add an extra guard: when forcing early-fill, respect per-GPU token-residual budget = free_ram_tokens * 0.6, so we don't blow OOM.

sami: implementation sketch (pseudo):
```
// on batcher tick
kernel = choose_kernel(profile)
lat = kernel.median_token_latency
wallet = base_wallet * (lat / baseline_lat)
if median_batch_size < 4 and p95_lat > threshold:
  wallet = min(wallet * 1.4, gpu_token_cap)
```

ops-jen: timeline? can we rollout to canary tomorrow? need perf regression guardrails in console and a rollback hook.

mike: canary on a subset of rerank endpoints (10% traffic) + perf-bot watches p50/p95 and tokens/sec; auto rollback if p95 regresses >10% for 10m.

jia: also add kernel-telemetry tag so we can correlate kernel-mix -> batch-size. currently that mapping is only in low-level logs.

sami: good call. action items:
- jami (mike) to add adaptive wallet multiplier + gpu_token_cap guard (PR by EOD)
- jia to add kernel-mix telemetry and a console dashboard tile
- ops-jen to configure canary + perf-bot rollback thresholds
- sami to run a short simulation to sanity-check wallet scaling on synthetic arrival patterns

mike: will do. will include a tiny sim harness in PR to show expected median batch sizes across kernel latency curves.

perf-bot: note: create incident if auto-rollback triggers twice in 24h

sami: thanks team. will post short follow-up with the sim outputs and a staging run tomorrow. :thumbsup:
